transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Happy to see so many of you online, uh, quick housekeeping - we will record this. Slides up on share: internal.link/q2-deck. Hi from me, Ethan, Priya, Liam, Sofia, and a few other execs are on.
[00:28] Ethan Park: Quick plug — if you're late, the recording and the deck will be in #all-hands. We'll start with Q2 highlights. Priya, you want to kick us off?
[00:45] Priya Rao: Yeah, sure. Q2 was solid, we hit 24% ARR growth quarter over quarter, pipeline healthy. A few big things: latency improvements on the serving runtime — avg p95 down ~12% for typical text-gen workloads; Dedicated committed deals up 3x vs Q1, and Private pilot traction with two regulated customers. There were also some nasty tail latency spikes early in June that we debugged — related to KV cash invalidation (transcript note: KV cache) and a bad sharding heuristic.
[01:20] Liam O'Connor: To add, a couple of big customer wins — FinTech X signed a Dedicated contract with a 12-month commit, and HealthCo is moving ahead with a pilot for our Private on-prem package. Those moved our net-new ARR nicely.
[01:38] Maya Chen: Great — thanks. Context for everyone: runway remains healthy, burn roughly flat vs plan, and we're on track for the targets we shared at the start of the year. We do need to be pragmatic about hiring; Sofia will talk through that.
[01:58] Sofia Martinez: Yeah, quick update on people ops. We're shifting hiring focus to core eng and reliability — limited new roles in other teams for Q3. Also announcing some org adjustments: two new manager-level roles in infra and product to help with scale. We'll post the org chart and an FAQ in #announcements right after this. We expect 1:1s to be scheduled with affected folks next week.
[02:25] [crosstalk] Speaker 1: Uh, does this mean a hiring freeze?
[02:29] Sofia Martinez: Not a full freeze — it's a prioritization. We're pausing a handful of reqs and opening strategic ones. Details in the doc.
[02:38] Ethan Park: On infra — short story: we'll be migrating some of our serving fleet configuration to the new scheduler that improves kernel selection and reduces node fragmentation. That shaves cost and improves steady-state latency. Timeline is late July to mid-August for the first wave. I'll publish a short note with the migration steps and expected customer impact. There's also one thing: we'll do canary traffic on Dedicated first, then expand.
[03:05] Priya Rao: We also found one perf regression tied to an optimizer. Fix landed last week, rollouts in staging look good. We'll be conservative with the rollout to Dedicated customers — canary followed by A/B ramp.
[03:20] Maya Chen: Security — update?
[03:22] Liam O'Connor: SOC two progress — we completed remediation of outstanding items from the last audit, waiting on one control verif that should complete this month. There are still a couple of doc items, but we expect SOC 2 Type II in Q3. For Private customers, we've added a KMS integration pattern and improved audit logging in the control plane.
[03:45] Priya Rao: Note: SAML/SSO and RBAC improvements shipped in the console last sprint. Some of those were requested by enterprise accounts doing compliance reviews. Also improved per-route tracing so you can see token-level latency and cost in the console.
[04:05] [00:04:05] Staff question (Speaker 2): On Dedicated autoscaling — can we expect more predictable burst capacity?
[04:10] Ethan Park: Yes. We're updating the autoscale policy engine to allow configured burst windows and priorities by queue. The new policy gives more predictable throughput and also exposes the cost tradeoffs. Priya is owning SLA definitions for that.
[04:28] Priya Rao: We aim to publish a draft SLA for Dedicated autoscale next week. It will include throughput buckets, burst limits, and fallback model tiers so customers don't hit catastrophic failures if capacity is exhausted.
[04:44] Maya Chen: Product roadmap highlight — Liam?
[04:46] Liam O'Connor: Shipping in Q3: better Optimize recommendations (auto-tune batching and quant profiles by workload), structured outputs for function/tool calling in the API, and a simpler Private deployment installer for on-prem. We also prioritized improving developer DX — docs site refresh and more SDK examples.
[05:04] [00:05:04] Speaker 3: Any notes on unit economics?
[05:07] Maya Chen: Unit economics improved slightly this quarter thanks to batching improvements and some kernel-level gains. We're still focusing on lowering per-token cost without increasing p95 latency. That's the tradeoff — latency vs cost — and I'm glad the engineering team is doing work there.
[05:22] Ethan Park: Quick nuance: some quant profiles reduce cost but introduce slight quality delta. We're shipping a tooling piece in Optimize that helps teams validate quality against eval sets before applying quant profiles broadly.
[05:38] [00:05:38] Speaker 4 (new hire): Hi — super quick, congrats on the SOC two progress — what's the expected impact on sales cycle?
[05:45] Liam O'Connor: SOC two Type II generally shortens sales cycle for enterprise customers because it reduces back-and-forth on controls. Expect a modest improvement in close times for regulated verticals.
[05:56] Maya Chen: Ok next section — wins and shoutouts. Big thanks to infra and runtime teams for the kernel selection work that reduced our AWS GPU hours. Shoutout to SE team for the HealthCo pilot runway.
[06:10] [00:06:10] Priya Rao: Shoutout to the benchmarking team — the new harness for continuous perf runs flagged the KV cash issue early in June and that saved us lots of debugging time.
[06:24] Maya Chen: Now we'll do leadership AMA — submit questions in the Q&A panel. We'll take the most upvoted ones.
[06:34] [00:06:34] Q&A Moderator (Speaker 5): Top question: "What does success look like for Q3?"
[06:40] Maya Chen: Good question. For Q3 success: 1) move key Dedicated customers to new autoscale with SLA, 2) close two Private pilots into paid contracts, 3) finish SOC 2 Type II, and 4) reduce p95 latency by another ~8% on our core gen workload.
[07:00] [00:07:00] Speaker 6: On the Dedicated pricing — any changes?
[07:03] Liam O'Connor: No list price changes planned; we're launching more flexible commit tiers and burst options which will change effective pricing by usage but not the published list.
[07:16] [00:07:16] Speaker 7: Are we expanding to new regions?
[07:18] Ethan Park: We're evaluating APAC expansion; procurement and partner terms are the blocker. We have a pilot region candidate but won't announce until contracts are in place.
[07:30] [00:07:30] Speaker 8: Question on Private deployment air-gap support?
[07:33] Priya Rao: Yes, the on-prem package now has air-gapped options. We added a one-time installer and support flow. There are still a few manual steps for cert rotation, but docs will be updated.
[07:48] [00:07:48] Speaker 9: Do we have a timeline for docs refresh?
[07:50] Liam O'Connor: Docs refresh starts next month; aim to complete by end of Q3. We'll prioritize guided quickstarts for Private and Dedicated autoscale configs.
[08:02] [00:08:02] Speaker 10: Is there any impact to existing Hosted customers from the infra migration?
[08:06] Ethan Park: Minimal. The first wave is Dedicated canaries; Hosted will be moved after we validate canary results. We'll have rolling updates and fallback policies. If you see odd behavior, file a ticket in #infra-ops.
[08:19] [00:08:19] Speaker 11: Could you talk a bit about benchmarking and the public numbers?
[08:22] Priya Rao: We plan to publish an updated benchmark set later in Q3; the internal numbers outperformed what we had publicly because of some kernel optimization. We'll sanitize and publish a reproducible benchmark focusing on latency and cost across common seq lengths.
[08:40] [00:08:40] Maya Chen: Alright, last few items — org changes recap and comp update timing. Sofia?
[08:45] Sofia Martinez: Org changes will be announced in the doc + a live Q&A for impacted teams on Thursday. Compensation cycles remain unchanged; we're not doing a company-wide comp refresh this quarter. Managers will discuss role changes in 1:1s.
[09:03] [00:09:03] Speaker 12: Any update on support SLAs and console retention?
[09:06] Liam O'Connor: We're evaluating increased retention (logs/traces) as a paid add-on. Support SLAs will be part of the Enterprise add-on; we will share tiers in the pricing doc.
[09:18] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Quick closing note: leadership is excited about the momentum, but also pragmatic — optimize for sustainable growth, really tighten focus on the work that moves the metrics we care about.
[09:32] [00:09:32] Ethan Park: I'll follow up with the infra migration note and a risk register. Priya will share the Dedicated autoscale SLA draft. Sofia will post org changes.
[09:44] [00:09:44] Maya Chen: Ok, we'll stop there. Thanks for coming. Recording and deck in #all-hands. See you next month.
[10:00] [END]
